title: Pt. Leo Estate Sculpture Park
summary: Australia's largest privately owned outdoor sculpture park: 16.5 acres, 60+ contemporary works, two walking loops, all set inside a working winery. Open daily 11am to 5pm.
priceRange: $15 adult; $8 concession; $30 family (2 adults + 2 children 12-17); free under 12
suitableFor: Art lovers; Families; Visitors; Wine enthusiasts
accessibilityNotes: Paved and gravel paths, mostly accessible; check with venue for specific needs
weatherDependency: Mostly weather independent, outdoor sculptures in all weather
nearbyAttractions: Pt. Leo cellar door; Merricks beach; Peninsula wineries
suggestedItineraryPairing: Combine with wine tasting at Pt. Leo cellar door; add winery lunch at Laura restaurant
editorVerdict: Australia's biggest privately owned outdoor sculpture park, and one of the few cultural attractions on the Peninsula that genuinely earns the comparison to anything in Melbourne.
editorNote:
Sixteen and a half acres of landscaped grounds wrapped around a working winery, planted with over sixty contemporary sculptures. There is a short loop (1.9km, about thirty minutes) and a long loop (3km, an hour), both gentle, both walkable in normal shoes. The collection is serious: international and Australian work that would not look out of place at the NGV.

The practical move is to arrive at 11am opening, walk the long loop while the light is good, then collapse into Pt. Leo's cellar door or Laura restaurant for lunch. Family pricing makes it the rare Peninsula cultural day that doesn't punish you for bringing kids. Bring sunscreen, hats, and proper walking shoes; the grass is the grass.

Open daily 11am to 5pm, last entry 4:30pm. $15 adult, kids under 12 free, $30 for a family of four.
